### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-owner-wall-bypass.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx`  _(via computeLayeredRlsFilter (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via computeLayeredRlsFilter (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-owner-wall-bypass.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1b34afcc82cbf730a4298b8e01f32f3705e88a26` — the merge of head `471f23549959eeb65866de78dc14eaf577262e68` into base `55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1b34afcc82cbf730a4298b8e01f32f3705e88a26 && git checkout 1b34afcc82cbf730a4298b8e01f32f3705e88a26
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c 471f23549959eeb65866de78dc14eaf577262e68 && git checkout -B drift-repro 55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c && git merge --no-ff 471f23549959eeb65866de78dc14eaf577262e68

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `471f23549959eeb65866de78dc14eaf577262e68`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-rls-filter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-owner-wall-bypass.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-owner-wall-bypass.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/plugin-driver-external-object.spike.test.ts + packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/tenant-layer.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/external-organization-scope.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts (`getObjectSecurityMeta`, the read-filter and write-wall callers), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.external-object-organization-scope-declared.ts, .changeset/sec-hardening-g-external-object-organization-scope.md

Inputs: the PR body, its file list, the net diff against the merge base `987ff33b88`, the check-runs on the head, and the ruling (maintainer, 2026-11-04, option A). Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` at line start in the PR body and the changeset), so the floor is every path of the diff outside the prose faces; the scope above adds the code the hunks cite.

Check-runs on the head: every check is completed and green or an expected skip; none is still running. `Check Changeset` is green (the changeset is this PR's own). `Lint & Repo Gates` is green, which includes the ADR-0087 registration gate re-validating the marker.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The stand-down condition catches exactly the undeclared-external deny and nothing else.** `deniedForUndeclaredExternalScope` is `verdict.kind === 'deny' && input.externalOrganizationScopeUndeclared === true`. Read in `computeTenantLayer0Verdict` (`packages/core`): the ladder answers `none` for the `single` posture and for a tenancy-disabled object before it reads the flag, and when it does read the flag set it returns `deny` ahead of every other rung. So whenever the flag is set under a wall the deny is that rung's, and whenever the deny is another rung's (the org-less session under `isolated`, the empty access set under `group`) the flag is unset, because `externalOrganizationScopeOf` answers `null` for every local object and `walled`/`shared` for an external object that declared. The two facts are therefore equivalent to "this deny is the configuration-defect deny", and the condition is exact. Tested on the cases asked:
   - local objects: flag unset, the owner still crosses the equality, the union and the org-less deny (test CONTROL, local object);
   - declared-walled external: `walled`, flag unset, the owner crosses, a member keeps the equality (test CONTROL);
   - an org-less owner on an undeclared external: the undeclared rung returns before the org-less rung, so the deny is the undeclared one and stands (pinned);
   - `group` and `isolated`: pinned; `single`: `none` before the flag, the branch is never entered (CONTROL);
   - delegated reads: `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` computes the delegator's own layered filter through the same function, so a delegator who is the owner meets the stand-down too;
   - explain, count and aggregate: `explain-engine.ts` and `security-plugin-explain-access.ts` call the same function, and every operation other than insert/update/delete is read-class in it, so count and aggregate take the same branch;
   - by-id reads: `getReadFilter` goes through `computeRlsFilter` into the same function; the by-id write pre-image carries the write operation and was walled already.
   `isVerifiedPlatformOwnerSession` has one consumer in the tree, this branch, so there is no second door for the owner's crossing to lift the verdict elsewhere. The `tenant-field-unenforceable` declaration is folded into the same flag by `externalOrganizationScopeIsUndeclared`, so a foreign `tenancy.tenantField` on an external object meets the same stand-down; that is the rule the boot refusal and the D3 entry already state for it, and the PR's prose ("states no organization scope the wall can enforce") covers it.
2. **The recorded verdict is honest.** When the stand-down holds the function returns the computed `{ layer0: RLS_DENY_FILTER, tenantLayer0Verdict: { kind: 'deny' }, crossedByPlatformAdmin }` untouched; `crossedByPlatformAdmin` is `false` there because it requires `kind === 'none'`. The verdict the engine reads and the filter the query carries are the same deny, so a reader learns nothing from a wall that still stands, and no crossing is logged (pinned: no bypass event, no `sys_user` read). The ADR-0095 D3 platform-admin crossing was already behind the undeclared rung on `main` (#29867), so this diff makes the owner's crossing consistent with it rather than introducing a new ordering.
3. **The ablation is the right instrument and read the right way:** replacing the condition with `true` reddened the three owner cases and (h5c) and nothing else; restored, all green with a clean tree. The pins fail for the reason the PR claims.
4. **The ADR-0087 marker `not-required (already-registered external-object-organization-scope-declared)` is right.** The entry exists at the merge base and at the head (`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.external-object-organization-scope-declared.ts`), which is the category's own test (named id resolves at HEAD and already existed at base). Its `replacement` prescribes the three declarations, which is the whole remedy here; nothing an author writes changes, so no new entry. The changeset carries exactly one marker, both declaration lines and the BREAKING section with who moves and the fix, as AGENTS.md step 3 requires of a breaking changeset.
5. **§6 holds.** Title, body, changeset and every test name state the rule ("reads as empty for every caller, the platform owner included", "the deny sentinel", "no crossing is logged"). No advisory id, no attack wording. The only "bypass" tokens are pre-existing identifiers (`platform-owner-wall-bypass.ts`, `PLATFORM_OWNER_WALL_BYPASS_EVENT`) carried over, not new wording.
6. **One prose claim in the PR body is inaccurate, not in the changeset.** The body says the texts "already on `main`" include ADR-0015 §10; the §10 amendment is in #29866 (docs, Tier H), still open and unmerged. The two code texts cited are on `main` (the D3 entry's "every read is denied at Layer 0"; the once-warning), and the changeset's "ADR-0015 §10 as amended" is the same citation the already-merged #29867 changeset and the D3 entry use. Correction for the body, not a must-fix.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-security`: `Metadata-protocol: none` is true (the three declarations an author writes are the ones `main` accepts, unchanged), and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition (AGENTS.md step 3). `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is true: nothing is widened, and one principal's reads narrow. Level, lines and marker agree.

**The dev's open question, A or B: A — keep `!` and `no (narrowing)`.** The arm's reference is the published accept set (clause2-line header: "a diff that NARROWS a published accept set"), and the published release is `@objectstack/plugin-security@18.3.0` (tag on `main`), which carries no undeclared-external verdict; there, the owner's read of such an object crossed the wall. On `main` after #29867 the #12974 crossing still lifted the undeclared deny for the owner, which is what the three owner cases and (h5c) measure under ablation. So this PR, not #29867, is the diff that takes the owner's published read away; the unreleased #29867 note describes the object's deny without naming the owner, and a note that is pending does not turn a later narrowing into a non-change. Two BREAKING notes in one release, each naming who moves, is the honest CHANGELOG. The battery the `!` owes was run at the head's source (417 files, 3462 passed). Under B the changeset would ship a narrowing with no banner, which is the shape the arm exists to prevent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev open question (A vs B): answered above, A.
- The ADR-0015 §10 text this PR and the D3 entry cite lands through #29866, Tier H, by the maintainer's hand; the ruling of 2026-11-04 (the owner included) is newer than that draft, so the maintainer may want the §10 text to name the owner when landing it. Not owed by this PR.
- `Skills-docs: none` stands on the two code texts on `main`; the body's "already on main" sentence should drop the ADR until #29866 lands (prose correction for the seat's ACCEPT).
- The spike file's `test-budget` header line is updated for the seventh (h) case; the budget value is unchanged.
- The author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); no out-of-relay login to name.

### ④ Design judgment

- `security-plugin-rls-filter.ts` against the ruling: the stand-down is one condition at the one crossing, keyed on the verdict and the input fact rather than on the object's shape re-derived, so it cannot disagree with the ladder that produced the deny; the owner probe is not consulted, so a stood-down read costs no `sys_user` row. The recorded verdict stays `deny`. Holds against the ruling (option A) and against the texts on `main` that already state the rule for every caller.
- `platform-owner-wall-bypass.ts` header: names the one verdict the read crossing does not lift, pointing at where the stand-down lives. Holds.
- Narrowing against the published spec on `main`: it does not take a declared capability away from a metadata author; it makes the platform's own refusal (the D3 entry's "every read is denied at Layer 0") real for the one principal it had not reached. The migration is the existing entry's remedy.
- Tests: the shared harness gains an optional `schema` instead of a new file, the new describe sits beside the crossing's existing pins, and each case names the rule; the controls (declared-walled, local, member, `single`) are the cases that make the stand-down's exactness a measurement rather than a reading. The spike's (h5c) checks the deny reaches the remote on the real `isolated` boot and keeps the declared-walled crossing as its control. The scenario the PR is accepted against is covered.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec-hardening-s`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: PASS**
